tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

# AGENTS.md - JSHack Field Manual

JSHack is a zero-dependency browser roguelike: pure JavaScript, pure ES modules,
ECS architecture, Deno tooling. This file is optimized for coding agents. Prefer
the commands below over manual spelunking.

Deeper docs:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [SEPARATION_MANIFEST.md](docs/architecture/SEPARATION_MANIFEST.md)
- [RUNTIME_TOPOLOGY_DOCTRINE.md](docs/architecture/RUNTIME_TOPOLOGY_DOCTRINE.md)
- [TEN_COMMANDMENTS.md](docs/architecture/TEN_COMMANDMENTS.md)
- [ecs-js/AGENTS.md](src/lib/ecs-js/AGENTS.md)

---

## Hard Laws

- **No build step.** Pure ES modules. No webpack, babel, JSX, TypeScript, or
  bundling.
- **Deno, not Node.** Tests and tools run with Deno. Default test command:
  `deno test --allow-read`.
- **JavaScript only.** Keep source as `.js` / `.mjs`.
- **Mobile-first.** Touch is primary; desktop keyboard is secondary.
- **Separation is law.** `rules/` never imports `display/` or `bridge/`;
  `display/` never imports `rules/`; `bridge/` projects read-only rule state.
- **No system-to-system calls.** Systems communicate with `world.emit` /
  `world.on`; scheduler owns ordering.
- **New events use concrete event classes.** Any new event contract must define
  a concrete `EcsEvent` class and emit an instance with
  `world.emit(new Event(...))`. Do not introduce string-only events or parallel
  string re-emits for new contracts.
- **Touched listener installers use canonical extensions.** Any new listener
  installer, or any existing listener installer touched during a task, must use
  `defineExtension(...)` and `world.install(...)` for idempotent installation.
  Do not add new bespoke symbol-guard installers.
- **No swallowed event failures.** Do not add `emitSafe`-style wrappers around
  `world.emit`.
- **No new world-attached state.** Do not attach simulation state to `world`
  with symbol or property keys (`world[...]`, `ctx.world[...]`). Use ECS
  components for state; when the state is genuinely world-scoped, model it as an
  explicit singleton entity/component and document the allowance. Existing
  world-attached state is a ratcheted architecture debt tracked by
  `ratchets/worldStateAttachmentRatchet.test.mjs`.
- **Determinism is sacred.** In rules simulation use `world.rand()`, never
  `Math.random()`. No timers/fetch/promises/async in systems.
- **Integer grid only.** World coords may be negative. Do not clamp to `>= 0`;
  normalize with `Number.isFinite(v) ? (v | 0) : fallback`.
- **One canonical path.** Spawn, damage, spell cast, status application,
  inventory transfer, and materialization paths must delegate to the canonical
  implementation.
- **Runtime multiplicity is child entities.** Runtime
  effects/procs/sockets/enchantments are child topology, not arrays on parent
  components.
- **ECS-js is vendored.** Do not edit `src/lib/ecs-js/` unless fixing the ECS
  library itself.
- **Authoring discipline.** Do not touch unrelated code. Do not make changes
  that do nothing. Always match the formatting preferences that already exist;
  be a chameleon.
- **Commit messages.** Every commit message must be lowercase and use a
  conventional type prefix such as `feat:`, `docs:`, `fix:`, `arch:`,
  `refactor:`, `test:`, `perf:`, `ci:`, or `chore:`.
- **Do not format code unless explicitly requested.** Do not run `deno fmt` or
  any other formatter as part of implementation or verification. Preserve the
  existing formatting and keep diffs limited to the requested functional edits.
- **Search before writing.** Extend existing patterns. Do exactly what was
  asked; no opportunistic content wiring or unrelated cleanup.
- **New authored content targets new runs.** Do not add migrations or repair
  paths for existing saved runs when adding quests, landmarks, dungeon
  entrances, or other authored world content. New content is expected to
  appear in newly generated runs; validate the fresh-run path instead.
- **Capture skills incrementally.** When a task reveals a reusable tool,
  process, authoring path, verification command, or failure mode, record the
  proven practice in the smallest relevant `.agents/skills/` guide as part of
  the task or its immediate follow-up. Do not make broad skills coverage a
  prerequisite for feature work, and do not document speculative patterns.
- **Verify in proportion to the change.** Run focused tests and guardrails that
  cover the touched behavior. Do not run the full runtime suite by default; it
  is allowed only when explicitly requested or when the change genuinely needs
  broad regression coverage. Always report what was run and any known or
  observed failures.
- **Content authoring comes first.** When adding content-facing behavior,
  prefer small authored definitions, generic affordances, and reusable engine
  surfaces over bespoke wiring. If a feature needs UI or interaction glue, ask
  whether `defineInteractable()`, content DSLs, or an existing canonical
  pipeline should own it before adding one-off main/display code.

## Agent Commands

Run these before guessing.

### Guardrail Tasks

Prefer these Deno tasks over hand-assembled command strings:

```bash
deno task check
deno task guard:architecture
deno task guard:events
deno task guard:death
deno task guard:tools
deno task ratchet:world-state
```

- `check` runs the architecture and event doctrine guardrails.
- `guard:architecture` runs agent health, import boundaries, and architecture
  ratchet tests.
- `guard:events` runs event doctrine ratchets and prints the event bus summary.
- `guard:death` runs the focused death pipeline/domain migration suite.
- `guard:tools` verifies the agent-facing tools and prints the system map.
- `ratchet:world-state` audits pre-existing `world[...]` simulation-state debt
  without making the normal architecture guard carry that allowlist.

Audit-only tasks:

```bash
deno task audit:health
deno task audit:systems
deno task audit:events
deno task audit:damaged
deno task audit:died
```

### Project Health

```bash
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/agent-health.mjs
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/import-boundary-report.mjs
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/system-map.mjs
```

`agent-health` summarizes boundary violations, remaining `emitSafe` refs,
nondeterminism hazards, generation-time async allowances, system counts, and
possible system-to-system calls. Classified allowances are context for agents;
headline hazards are the things to investigate first.

### Event Bus

```bash
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs --format summary --top 40
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs --format csv --event damaged
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs --format mermaid --event damaged
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs --producer-only --format summary --top 40
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs --consumer-only --format summary --top 40
```

Use producer-only events to find emitted behavior with no consumer. Use
consumer-only events to find stale listeners, dynamic producers, or missing
producers.

### System Map

```bash
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/system-map.mjs --format summary
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/system-map.mjs --format csv
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/system-map.mjs --phase effects
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/system-map.mjs --unregistered
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/system-map.mjs --missing-tests
```

Scheduler truth lives in [src/main/scheduler.js](src/main/scheduler.js). Some
imported-not-registered files are listener installers, not phase systems; audit
before deleting.

### Target Lookup

```bash
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/agent-target.mjs damaged --limit 80
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/content-id-audit.mjs goblin --limit 80
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/content-id-audit.mjs potion_water --limit 80
deno task audit:quests
```

`agent-target` is a ranked code search for events/functions/files/tests.
`content-id-audit` follows item, monster, spell, material, loot, visual, and
test references by ID.

`audit:quests` validates authored quest destinations using canonical fields:
tracker target, landmark entrance, and explicit monster IDs.

### Agent tool ownership

Every current `tools/` entry is classified in
[docs/architecture/AGENT_TOOL_OWNERSHIP.md](docs/architecture/AGENT_TOOL_OWNERSHIP.md).
Agent-facing deterministic inspection, runtime-proof, and monster-training
implementations are colocated with their owning skill under
`.agents/skills/<owner>/scripts/`. General repository/CI/developer tooling,
browser authoring tools, audio asset tooling, and other independent-lifecycle
utilities remain in `tools/` with their rationale recorded in that matrix.
There is one canonical implementation per moved tool; stable `deno task`
interfaces remain the compatibility boundary.

For the complete routing workflow, use
[`.agents/skills/agent-tools/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/agent-tools/SKILL.md).

### Runtime Proving and Performance

Use [`.agents/skills/runtime-tools/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/runtime-tools/SKILL.md)
when static inspection must be followed by a seeded headless run, agent-bridge
trace, scheduler profile, or performance baseline.

### Focused Tests

```bash
deno test --allow-read tests/separationBoundaries.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/determinismArchitectureGuards.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/schedulerArchitectureGuards.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/dealDamage.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/castSpell.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/interaction.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/movementRefactored.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/contentCatalogCanonical.test.mjs
```

Prefer the smallest meaningful verification set: changed test files, adjacent
behavior tests, architecture guardrails, and targeted audit tools. If you do run
broad runtime coverage, use `deno test --allow-read --no-check` and treat
pre-existing failures as baseline debt to report, not as permission to obscure
new failures.

is not the thing being tested.

```bash
rg -n "world\\.(on|emit)\\s*\\(" src --glob '!src/lib/**'

rg -n "Math\\.random|Date\\.now|setTimeout|setInterval|Promise|fetch|await" src/rules
rg -n "from ['\"].*display|from ['\"].*bridge" src/rules
rg -n "from ['\"].*rules" src/display
```

## Architecture Map

```text
rules/    deterministic simulation; no DOM, display, timers, async systems
bridge/   read-only projection from rules state to WorldView DTOs
display/  presentation only; reads WorldView and main-provided contracts
main/     wiring, lifecycle, input dispatch, scheduler setup
shared/   pure math/grid utilities; no ECS or DOM
lib/      vendored ecs-js and deity-js
content/  DSL-authored content definitions and content helpers
```

Five scheduler phases are declared in
[src/main/scheduler.js](src/main/scheduler.js):

```text
ai       intent producers
intents  movement/combat/use/cast/interaction consumers
effects  per-turn derived effects and world simulation
scripts  content DSL tick hooks
cleanup  entity removal, lifespan, spatial sync
```

The bridge contract is
[src/bridge/schema/worldView.js](src/bridge/schema/worldView.js). Display must
not push tags onto entity records; tag projection belongs in the bridge.

## Patterns That Matter

### Content-First Engine Work

The architecture exists to make strange rules cheap to author. Before adding a
new one-off interaction, modal, command, or UI bridge, look for the content
surface that should own it:

- `defineInteractable()` for object affordances, verbs, prompts, and hooks.
- Content DSL/catalog files for canonical item, monster, spell, and feature
  authoring.
- Existing rules pipelines for spawn, damage, use/apply, status, inventory, and
  transitions.

For item mechanic copy, authored prose must use placeholders for mechanical
values (for example `{duration}` or `{effect.damage.amount}`). Resolve those
values from the canonical ability/effect/stat metadata; never duplicate live
numbers inside English descriptions or display formats.

The standard is not "least code today." The standard is whether the next weird
rule becomes small, explicit, composable, deterministic, and inspectable.

### Incremental Skill Capture

Treat each completed issue as an opportunity to improve the next agent's
starting position. During implementation, note the canonical files and paths,
required tools or commands, architectural invariants, useful fixtures, and
failure modes that were discovered. After the behavior is proven, update the
smallest relevant skill—or create one only when a repeated workflow justifies
it—with those verified details and a focused validation recipe.

Skill capture is evidence-based documentation, not a parallel architecture
project. Keep feature delivery moving when a skill does not yet exist, and
avoid turning one issue into a repository-wide skills rewrite.

### Listener Installers

Use `defineExtension(...)` and `world.install(...)` for listener installers:

```js
import { defineExtension } from "../../lib/ecs-js/index.js";
import { FeatureHappened } from "../../events/FeatureHappened.js";

export const featureListeners = defineExtension(
  "jshack:domain:feature",
  (world) => {
    world.on(FeatureHappened, (event) => {});
  },
);
```

Install listeners with `world.install(featureListeners)` from `configureWorld()`
unless the feature is display/main wiring.

### New Systems

1. Add `src/rules/systems/mySystem.js`.
2. Register it in [src/main/scheduler.js](src/main/scheduler.js) in the right
   phase.
3. Add a focused test in `tests/`.
4. Run `deno test --allow-read tests/mySystem.test.mjs`.

### Spatial Queries

Use `forEachInRadius`, `forEachInRect`, or tile query helpers. Do not full-scan
`world.query()` for proximity-sensitive behavior.

### Spawning

Route through canonical archetypes/materialization helpers. Debug spawns,
dungeon population, and spawner children must have parity tests if they differ.

### Events

New event contracts must be concrete `EcsEvent` classes:

```js
import { EcsEvent } from "../lib/ecs-js/index.js";

export class FeatureHappened extends EcsEvent {
  constructor(payload = {}) {
    super();
    this.actorId = Number(payload.actorId || 0) | 0;
    Object.freeze(this);
  }
}

world.emit(new FeatureHappened({ actorId }));
```

If an event should be visible to display/audio/messages, verify the complete
producer/consumer wiring with:

```bash
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs --format csv --event event:name
```

---

## Red Tests

Tests can be stale. Do not make tests green by restoring old behavior unless the
user explicitly asks for that behavior.

Classify failures:

- **Real bug:** fix implementation.
- **Stale expectation:** update the test to current intended behavior.
- **Ambiguous:** stop and ask.

Prefer invariant tests over brittle snapshots: determinism, reachability,
bounds, parity, layer boundaries, canonical paths.

---

## Merge Checklist

- [ ] No build step or new dependency pipeline.
- [ ] No `Math.random()` in rules simulation.
- [ ] No `emitSafe` or swallowed event errors.
- [ ] No new `world[...]` / `ctx.world[...]` simulation state; use ECS
      components or an explicit singleton component.
- [ ] No direct system-to-system calls.
- [ ] No illegal layer imports.
- [ ] New or touched listeners use `defineExtension(...)` and
      `world.install(...)`.
- [ ] New systems are registered and tested.
- [ ] Spawn paths use canonical constructors/materializers.
- [ ] Event wiring checked with `.agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs`.
- [ ] Agent health checked with `.agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/agent-health.mjs`.
- [ ] Focused tests and relevant guardrails were run and reported.

```bash
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/system-map.mjs --phase effects
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/system-map.mjs --unregistered
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/system-map.mjs --missing-tests
```

Scheduler truth lives in [src/main/scheduler.js](src/main/scheduler.js). Some
imported-not-registered files are listener installers, not phase systems; audit
before deleting.

### Target Lookup

```bash
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/agent-target.mjs damaged --limit 80
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/content-id-audit.mjs goblin --limit 80
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/content-id-audit.mjs potion_water --limit 80
deno task audit:quests
```

`agent-target` is a ranked code search for events/functions/files/tests.
`content-id-audit` follows item, monster, spell, material, loot, visual, and
test references by ID.

`audit:quests` validates authored quest destinations using canonical fields:
tracker target, landmark entrance, and explicit monster IDs.

### Agent tool ownership

Every current `tools/` entry is classified in
[docs/architecture/AGENT_TOOL_OWNERSHIP.md](docs/architecture/AGENT_TOOL_OWNERSHIP.md).
Agent-facing deterministic inspection, runtime-proof, and monster-training
implementations are colocated with their owning skill under
`.agents/skills/<owner>/scripts/`. General repository/CI/developer tooling,
browser authoring tools, audio asset tooling, and other independent-lifecycle
utilities remain in `tools/` with their rationale recorded in that matrix.
There is one canonical implementation per moved tool; stable `deno task`
interfaces remain the compatibility boundary.

For the complete routing workflow, use
[`.agents/skills/agent-tools/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/agent-tools/SKILL.md).

### Runtime Proving and Performance

Use [`.agents/skills/runtime-tools/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/runtime-tools/SKILL.md)
when static inspection must be followed by a seeded headless run, agent-bridge
trace, scheduler profile, or performance baseline.

### Focused Tests

```bash
deno test --allow-read tests/separationBoundaries.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/determinismArchitectureGuards.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/schedulerArchitectureGuards.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/dealDamage.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/castSpell.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/interaction.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/movementRefactored.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/contentCatalogCanonical.test.mjs
```

Prefer the smallest meaningful verification set: changed test files, adjacent
behavior tests, architecture guardrails, and targeted audit tools. If you do run
broad runtime coverage, use `deno test --allow-read --no-check` and treat
pre-existing failures as baseline debt to report, not as permission to obscure
new failures.

Plain `deno test --allow-read` may fail during type-check on non-game packaging
scripts before tests run. Use `--no-check` for runtime coverage when type-check
is not the thing being tested.

### Fast Greps

```bash
rg -n "world\\.(on|emit)\\s*\\(" src --glob '!src/lib/**'
rg -n "registerSystem\\(|install[A-Za-z0-9_]+\\(" src/main/scheduler.js
rg -n "Math\\.random|Date\\.now|setTimeout|setInterval|Promise|fetch|await" src/rules
rg -n "from ['\"].*display|from ['\"].*bridge" src/rules
rg -n "from ['\"].*rules" src/display
```

---

## Architecture Map

```text
rules/    deterministic simulation; no DOM, display, timers, async systems
bridge/   read-only projection from rules state to WorldView DTOs
display/  presentation only; reads WorldView and main-provided contracts
main/     wiring, lifecycle, input dispatch, scheduler setup
shared/   pure math/grid utilities; no ECS or DOM
lib/      vendored ecs-js and deity-js
content/  DSL-authored content definitions and content helpers
```

Five scheduler phases are declared in
[src/main/scheduler.js](src/main/scheduler.js):

```text
ai       intent producers
intents  movement/combat/use/cast/interaction consumers
effects  per-turn derived effects and world simulation
scripts  content DSL tick hooks
cleanup  entity removal, lifespan, spatial sync
```

The bridge contract is
[src/bridge/schema/worldView.js](src/bridge/schema/worldView.js). Display must
not push tags onto entity records; tag projection belongs in the bridge.

---

## Common Locations

| Need                 | Start Here                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Scheduler order      | [src/main/scheduler.js](src/main/scheduler.js)                                                                                                         |
| WorldView projection | [src/bridge/schema/worldView.js](src/bridge/schema/worldView.js)                                                                                       |
| Systems              | [src/rules/systems/](src/rules/systems/)                                                                                                               |
| Components           | [src/rules/components/](src/rules/components/)                                                                                                         |
| Monsters             | [src/content/monsters/](src/content/monsters/), [src/rules/data/monsters.js](src/rules/data/monsters.js)                                               |
| Items                | [src/content/items/](src/content/items/), [src/rules/data/itemCatalog.js](src/rules/data/itemCatalog.js)                                               |
| Spells               | [src/rules/data/spells.js](src/rules/data/spells.js), [src/rules/scripts/spells.js](src/rules/scripts/spells.js)                                       |
| Interaction payloads | [src/rules/content/interaction/interactPayloads.js](src/rules/content/interaction/interactPayloads.js)                                                 |
| Damage               | [src/rules/utils/dealDamage.js](src/rules/utils/dealDamage.js)                                                                                         |
| Status semantics     | [src/rules/utils/effectSemantics.js](src/rules/utils/effectSemantics.js), [src/rules/utils/statusFacade.js](src/rules/utils/statusFacade.js)           |
| Spatial queries      | [src/rules/utils/spatialIndex.js](src/rules/utils/spatialIndex.js)                                                                                     |
| Inventory            | [src/rules/utils/inventoryFacade.js](src/rules/utils/inventoryFacade.js), [src/rules/utils/inventoryVirtuals.js](src/rules/utils/inventoryVirtuals.js) |
| Materials/gems       | [src/rules/data/materials.js](src/rules/data/materials.js), [src/rules/data/gems.js](src/rules/data/gems.js)                                           |
| Dungeon tiles/FOV    | [src/rules/environment/dungeon/](src/rules/environment/dungeon/)                                                                                       |
| Quests/dialog        | [src/rules/quests/](src/rules/quests/), [src/rules/dialogues/](src/rules/dialogues/)                                                                   |
| Display event wiring | [src/display/ui/wiring/](src/display/ui/wiring/)                                                                                                       |
| Audio wiring         | [src/display/audio/](src/display/audio/)                                                                                                               |

---

## Patterns That Matter

### Content-First Engine Work

The architecture exists to make strange rules cheap to author. Before adding a
new one-off interaction, modal, command, or UI bridge, look for the content
surface that should own it:

- `defineInteractable()` for object affordances, verbs, prompts, and hooks.
- Content DSL/catalog files for canonical item, monster, spell, and feature
  authoring.
- Existing rules pipelines for spawn, damage, use/apply, status, inventory, and
  transitions.

For item mechanic copy, authored prose must use placeholders for mechanical
values (for example `{duration}` or `{effect.damage.amount}`). Resolve those
values from the canonical ability/effect/stat metadata; never duplicate live
numbers inside English descriptions or display formats.

The standard is not "least code today." The standard is whether the next weird
rule becomes small, explicit, composable, deterministic, and inspectable.

### Incremental Skill Capture

Treat each completed issue as an opportunity to improve the next agent's
starting position. During implementation, note the canonical files and paths,
required tools or commands, architectural invariants, useful fixtures, and
failure modes that were discovered. After the behavior is proven, update the
smallest relevant skill—or create one only when a repeated workflow justifies
it—with those verified details and a focused validation recipe.

Skill capture is evidence-based documentation, not a parallel architecture
project. Keep feature delivery moving when a skill does not yet exist, and
avoid turning one issue into a repository-wide skills rewrite.

### Listener Installers

Use `defineExtension(...)` and `world.install(...)` for listener installers:

```js
import { defineExtension } from "../../lib/ecs-js/index.js";
import { FeatureHappened } from "../../events/FeatureHappened.js";

export const featureListeners = defineExtension(
  "jshack:domain:feature",
  (world) => {
    world.on(FeatureHappened, (event) => {});
  },
);
```

Install listeners with `world.install(featureListeners)` from `configureWorld()`
unless the feature is display/main wiring.

### New Systems

1. Add `src/rules/systems/mySystem.js`.
2. Register it in [src/main/scheduler.js](src/main/scheduler.js) in the right
   phase.
3. Add a focused test in `tests/`.
4. Run `deno test --allow-read tests/mySystem.test.mjs`.

### Spatial Queries

Use `forEachInRadius`, `forEachInRect`, or tile query helpers. Do not full-scan
`world.query()` for proximity-sensitive behavior.

### Spawning

Route through canonical archetypes/materialization helpers. Debug spawns,
dungeon population, and spawner children must have parity tests if they differ.

### Events

New event contracts must be concrete `EcsEvent` classes:

```js
import { EcsEvent } from "../lib/ecs-js/index.js";

export class FeatureHappened extends EcsEvent {
  constructor(payload = {}) {
    super();
    this.actorId = Number(payload.actorId || 0) | 0;
    Object.freeze(this);
  }
}

world.emit(new FeatureHappened({ actorId }));
```

If an event should be visible to display/audio/messages, verify the complete
producer/consumer wiring with:

```bash
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs --format csv --event event:name
```

---

## Red Tests

Tests can be stale. Do not make tests green by restoring old behavior unless the
user explicitly asks for that behavior.

Classify failures:

- **Real bug:** fix implementation.
- **Stale expectation:** update the test to current intended behavior.
- **Ambiguous:** stop and ask.

Prefer invariant tests over brittle snapshots: determinism, reachability,
bounds, parity, layer boundaries, canonical paths.

---

## Merge Checklist

- [ ] No build step or new dependency pipeline.
- [ ] No `Math.random()` in rules simulation.
- [ ] No `emitSafe` or swallowed event errors.
- [ ] No new `world[...]` / `ctx.world[...]` simulation state; use ECS
      components or an explicit singleton component.
- [ ] No direct system-to-system calls.
- [ ] No illegal layer imports.
- [ ] New or touched listeners use `defineExtension(...)` and
      `world.install(...)`.
- [ ] New systems are registered and tested.
- [ ] Spawn paths use canonical constructors/materializers.
- [ ] Event wiring checked with `.agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs`.
- [ ] Agent health checked with `.agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/agent-health.mjs`.
- [ ] Focused tests and relevant guardrails were run and reported.

issues.title: UX: Rebuild Inventory as an Icon Grid with Automatic Stacking and Fast Item Actions
issues.body:
## Thesis

Now that JS Hack has a canonical **item icon atlas**, the inventory should no longer read like a terminal-era list of text rows.

**Rebuild Inventory as a dense, readable, responsive icon grid**: recognizable item art, quantity badges, automatic stacking, meaningful sorting and filtering, and a first-class selected-item detail/action panel.

This should feel like a modern roguelike inventory while remaining unmistakably JS Hack. It is **not** a request for a Diablo-style spatial Tetris bag, nor a rewrite of the underlying ECS inventory architecture.

> **Icons for recognition. Stacks for clarity. Details on demand. Actions without friction.**

## Current implementation (read these first)

The existing implementation already has several important pieces:

- `src/display/ui/inventoryOverlay.js`: keyboard-driven **vertical text row list** with a details/actions pane, responsive one-/two-column *outer* layout, selection persistence, keyboard shortcuts, item actions, weight bar, equipped/pinned state, rarity, and quantity.
- `src/display/ui/atlasIcons.js` and `assets/icons/items/manifest.js` + `sheet.webp`: shared WebP item-icon atlas keyed by canonical item identities. Inventory rows currently use these icons primarily for **gem/enchantment modifiers**, not as the primary visual for every item.
- `src/main/ui/inventoryDataProvider.js`: constructs item display records (including `identity`) and calls `groupDisplayItems` before dispatching inventory data.
- `src/main/ui/itemGrouping.js`: already **visually coalesces equivalent display records**, sums counts, and preserves `entityIds`. Do not reinvent it without examining its grouping semantics.
- `src/rules/utils/inventoryFacade.js`: canonical ECS containment (`owner -> InventoryRoot -> item`), capacity accounting, and **existing conditional physical stack merging** during `addToInventory`. Keep all mutations behind the existing facade.
- `src/rules/components/Inventory.js`: capacity counts **distinct stacks**, not geometric cells. Encumbrance/weight is a separate mechanic.
- `src/main/wiring/itemName.js`: item display construction, identity and identification handling, affixes, enchants, gems, mechanics, descriptions, etc.
- `src/display/ui/inventoryUtils.js` and `src/display/ui/overlayUtils.js`: default actions, item detail rendering, and existing controls.

**Important distinction:** Visual grouping and physical entity merging are different. Both already exist. This issue is primarily a substantial **inventory UX overhaul**, with stacking correctness audited rather than blindly reimplemented.

## Desired experience

### 1. The grid

- Replace the **item-row list** with a real **multi-column grid of square/near-square item tiles**.
- Use the existing **32px canonical item artwork**, scaled cleanly with pixelated rendering (use `applyAtlasIcon` / `ITEM_ICON_ATLAS`).
- Each tile shows one primary item icon, a clear selected/focused state, and compact badges where needed.
- Adapt columns to available width on desktop/tablet/phone; tiles remain comfortably tappable on touch.
- Keep the existing item **detail + actions** panel. Desktop can show it beside the grid; compact layouts can put it below or reveal it contextually, without permanently consuming the whole viewport.
- Retain carry-weight/encumbrance information, with room for stack-slot usage (`used / capacity`) if accurately sourced.
- Distinguish an **icon grid** from the existing CSS grid that merely arranges list + detail panes.

### 2. Primary icon and item identity

- Resolve a tile's principal icon from the canonical item identity using the current atlas/manifest.
- Use sensible fallbacks when the atlas has no entry; never show a blank or broken tile.
- **Do not leak unidentified item identity via its icon.** Appearance/unknown category artwork should respect `identified` / identification rules, including unidentified potions, scrolls, wands, gems, and equipment.
- Keep the textual resolved name in detail/tooltip/accessibility labels, including unidentified state.
- Preserve rarity cues without using color as the sole indicator.
- Affix, enchantment, gem, and proc indicators may be compact overlays (or remain in selected details); do not bury the main item art in modifier clutter.
- Preserve equipment/pinned status indicators and cursed/unpaid/identified/coated/cooldown signals where appropriate.
- Be intentional about badge precedence; don't turn each tile into a tiny character sheet.

### 3. Automatic stacking — reuse, verify, make unmistakable

- Visually identical, *truly stack-compatible* items should occupy one tile with an unobtrusive `×N` quantity badge.
- No manual stacking/dragging required; acquiring another compatible item should update the tile immediately.
- Retain `entityIds` and accurate total quantities; do not fake `×N` with a count unrelated to actionable items.
- On use/consume/throw/drop/equip, update the correct backing entity/quantity and refresh the tile.
- Support split or quantity selection for stack-sensitive actions **where applicable to existing action rules**; don't assume `Drop` or `Throw` always means the entire stack.
- Avoid count inflation or disappearing items after partial consumption, equip/unequip, repeated pickup, save/load, or switching inventory screens.

**Stack compatibility is a correctness boundary, not a name equality test.** The current facade's `capacityStackKey` is largely identity-based except for charges, script state, and unpaid state; `groupDisplayItems` uses a richer display-equivalence key. Audit the differences. Do **not** physically merge items if doing so loses distinct state or behavior: beatitude/curses, unidentified state, durability/corrosion/wetness, charges, affixes, enchantments, gems/sockets, coatings, cooldowns, ownership/unpaid pricing, item-specific scripts, or any other meaningful per-entity metadata.

If current underlying merge rules are unsafe, fix them narrowly with regression tests or record a clearly scoped follow-up. **A UI grid must never delete a unique enchanted item by treating it as an ordinary duplicate.**

Capacity must continue to follow *canonical inventory rules* rather than tile count if visual grouping and capacity stacking have different definitions. Surface the distinction instead of silently redefining capacity.

### 4. Sorting, grouping, and discovery

- Provide predictable default ordering that puts frequently used items within reach (propose and implement an explicit stable policy; do not depend on arbitrary ECS iteration order).
- Offer quick category filters such as **All / Weapons & Gear / Consumables / Magic / Materials & Misc** as appropriate to actual catalog types. No forced taxonomy rewrite.
- Add a lightweight name search for large bags, using already-safe/displayed item names (do not search hidden canonical identities of unidentified items).
- Useful sort controls: **Type**, **Name**, **Rarity**, **Recent** (only if acquisition order is reliably available; otherwise omit), with clear stable tie-breaking.
- Counts and weight should reflect *all* carried inventory even when the grid is filtered.
- Empty-filter and zero-item states should be intelligible.
- Never require players to micro-organize manually just to avoid chaotic grid order.
- Preserve existing slot filters/character-menu tabs and quick-pin affordances.

### 5. Interaction and details

- **Single click/tap:** select tile and inspect its item details.
- **Double click / deliberate activation:** invoke the existing safe default item action; avoid accidental destructive actions on mobile.
- Preserve all existing action paths: **Use, Equip/Unequip, Apply/Socket, Identify, Throw, Drop, Pin, Set Spell**, plus relevant pickup actions.
- Keep existing affordances for curses, unpaid goods, charges, cooldowns, coatings, sockets, and affix/ability information.
- Do not change action intent/event contracts casually. Reuse the existing `ui:request*` dispatch paths and inventory facade.
- Preserve keyboard-first operation. Arrow keys navigate the grid spatially (left/right ±1, up/down ±column count), with Home/End, Enter, Escape, existing shortcuts and Tab behavior retained. No trap when focus moves into search/controls/detail.
- Preserve selection by stable identity/backing key through stacking, filtering, sort changes, pickup/use/drop, and overlay refreshes. If selected item disappears, choose the nearest sensible surviving tile.
- Provide clearly visible keyboard focus and hover/touch feedback. Focus must remain deterministic after a filtered/rendered update.
- Ensure the layout works with mouse, keyboard, touch, and smaller screens. Avoid scroll jumps or scroll trapping.
- Any optional drag/drop should be a convenience over the existing action pipeline, **not the only way to equip, drop, or rearrange**, and should not require a new spatial inventory model.

### 6. Visual hierarchy

A tile should communicate at a glance:
1. **What item is this?** (primary icon)
2. **How many?** (stack badge)
3. **How special?** (rarity/identification cues)
4. **Is it equipped/pinned/unpaid/affected?** (small status signals)

Everything else belongs in the **selected-item detail panel**, where we already have rich data and actions.

Avoid reproducing the current row's full textual metadata in miniature. The entire point is visual density with reduced clutter.

## Engineering constraints

- Presentation only where feasible; do **not** replace `InventoryRoot` / ECS hierarchy or introduce per-cell game-state ownership.
- Do not change carry-weight, item capacity, equipment, or stack rules by accident.
- Reuse `groupDisplayItems` and the current icon/identity machinery when sound; improve shared utilities instead of adding a second grouping implementation inside the overlay.
- Distinguish **item icon** from **modifier icons** and preserve identification secrecy.
- Preserve displayed descriptions and item interactions, including custom content-driven abilities.
- Render from authoritative provider snapshots; don't duplicate item rules inside the DOM.
- Don't assume all catalog items have atlas entries; test fallback coverage.
- Keep the underlying stacking and action behavior deterministic and save/load-safe.
- Favor small, reviewable components: grid renderer/tile component, pure item presentation/grouping helpers, input/navigation controller, and minimal provider changes rather than a monolithic overlay rewrite.
- Update existing tests rather than simply deleting old list-specific assertions.

## Implementation plan

### Phase A — Inventory behavior + icon coverage audit
- [ ] Read the current Inventory overlay, data provider, grouping helper, inventory facade, identity/identification, and atlas.
- [ ] Inventory current actions, shortcuts, visual states, and responsive behavior.
- [ ] Audit item atlas coverage and safe unknown/identified icon resolution.
- [ ] Audit real stack compatibility versus display grouping and capacity grouping; identify known stateful edge cases.
- [ ] Capture baseline behavior/tests before UI surgery.

### Phase B — Grid layout and interaction
- [ ] Replace vertical item rows with responsive icon tiles.
- [ ] Render primary item icons with fallback and identification safety.
- [ ] Add selection/focus, equipped/pinned/rarity/count badges.
- [ ] Retain weight/capacity and selected-item details/actions.
- [ ] Implement correct 2D keyboard navigation and mobile tap behavior.
- [ ] Persist selection and scroll position across updates.

### Phase C — Stacking, organization, and commands
- [ ] Integrate existing grouped display items with quantity tiles.
- [ ] Ensure automatic stack updates and safe backing-entity action routing.
- [ ] Define quantity behavior for Use/Throw/Drop and partial stacks.
- [ ] Add stable default order, category filters, name search, and supported sort controls.
- [ ] Preserve existing character-menu tabs and quick-pin interactions.
- [ ] Correct any confirmed unsafe physical merges without broad inventory-schema changes.

### Phase D — Polish, tests, and documentation
- [ ] Validate icon fidelity, badge contrast, tile density, responsive breakpoints.
- [ ] Verify desktop, mobile/touch, and keyboard operation.
- [ ] Verify all actions and item states, including unknown items, enchants, unpaid goods, and curses.
- [ ] Exercise large inventories and grouped counts with no severe rerender/performance regression.
- [ ] Run tests, fix regressions, and document behavior and known follow-ups.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Inventory is a **genuine icon tile grid**, not merely a two-column layout containing text rows.
- [ ] Canonical item art renders from the current WebP atlas, with safe text/category fallback.
- [ ] Unidentified items do not reveal hidden identities through icons, search, labels, or stack behavior.
- [ ] Compatible duplicates visually auto-stack with accurate quantity badges; state-distinct items remain distinct.
- [ ] No unique item, charge state, enhancement, payment state, or other relevant metadata is destroyed through stacking.
- [ ] Physical/capacity stacking remains correct; carried weight and capacity are unchanged.
- [ ] Consumptions, drops, throws, equipment changes, and partial-stack actions target the correct entity and quantity.
- [ ] Sorting, category filtering, and name search work predictably without losing selection.
- [ ] Selection and details remain usable with keyboard, mouse, and touch.
- [ ] Existing Use/Equip/Apply/Identify/Throw/Drop/Pin/Set Spell/pickup actions remain functional.
- [ ] Rarity, counts, equipment state, quick pins, curses, unpaid status, and meaningful modifiers remain discoverable.
- [ ] The grid is readable and performant on desktop and mobile.
- [ ] Current ECS containment, determinism, save/load, and gameplay mechanics are preserved.
- [ ] Relevant automated tests pass, with new coverage for grouping/stacking correctness and input navigation.

## Non-goals

- A geometric bag with differently sized item shapes.
- A new item-ownership, inventory-capacity, or equipment engine.
- A redesign of all chest/shop/ground inventories at once (reusable tiles are welcome, but scope this to the player Inventory screen).
- Broad item balance or stack-size rebalance.
- Requiring drag-and-drop to play.
- Changing content item identities, atlas coordinates, or asset formats unless a specific missing icon requires an intentional fallback/fix.

## Final design principle

> **The new icon system should finally make opening the backpack feel like looking through a collection of things, not reading a database table.**
>
> **Recognize it. Stack it. Inspect it. Use it.**
>
> Preserve JS Hack's unusual objects and all the weirdness underneath the icons.

1. **What item is this?** (primary icon)
2. **How many?** (stack badge)
3. **How special?** (rarity/identification cues)
4. **Is it equipped/pinned/unpaid/affected?** (small status signals)

- [ ] Current ECS containment, determinism, save/load, and gameplay mechanics are preserved.

- A geometric bag with differently sized item shapes.
- A new item-ownership, inventory-capacity, or equipment engine.
- A redesign of all chest/shop/ground inventories at once (reusable tiles are welcome, but scope this to the player Inventory screen).

- Requiring drag-and-drop to play.

> **The new icon system should finally make opening the backpack feel like looking through a collection of things, not reading a database table.**
>
> **Recognize it. Stack it. Inspect it. Use it.**

---
name: agent-tools
description: Use JSHack's deterministic inspection and architecture tools to locate behavior, verify boundaries, and gather evidence before changing code.
argument-hint: <question-or-target>
---

Use this skill when a task needs repository-wide discovery, architecture evidence,
event wiring analysis, scheduler mapping, content-ID tracing, or a health check.
These tools are read-only unless a command explicitly says otherwise. Their
canonical implementations live beside this guide in `scripts/`; invoke them
from the repository root and prefer the smallest output mode that answers the
question.

## Start with the question

Choose the route before searching broadly:

| Need | Tool | First command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Find a symbol, event, file, or test | `agent-target` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/agent-target.mjs TERM --limit 80` |
| Trace an item, monster, spell, material, loot, or visual ID | `content-id-audit` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/content-id-audit.mjs ID --limit 80` |
| Inventory item rarity slots and find legacy/mismatched labels | `item-rarity-audit` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/item-rarity-audit.mjs --gear-only --format csv` |
| Find proc-package gear missing authored Equip mechanics | `proc-gear-audit` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/proc-gear-audit.mjs --unconverted` |
| Compare same-slot gear and flag obvious strength outliers | `item-strength-audit` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/item-strength-audit.mjs --outliers --format csv` |
| Understand event producers and consumers | `event-bus-explorer` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs --format summary --top 40` |
| Validate a quest-backed dungeon | `quest-content-audit` | `deno task audit:quests` |
| Inspect one event contract | `event-bus-explorer` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs --format csv --event EVENT` |
| Map scheduler registration and phases | `system-map` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/system-map.mjs --format summary` |
| Find unregistered or untested systems | `system-map` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/system-map.mjs --unregistered` or `--missing-tests` |
| Check architecture hazards | `agent-health` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/agent-health.mjs` |
| Inspect import-layer violations | `import-boundary-report` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/import-boundary-report.mjs` |

## Evidence workflow

1. Run the narrowest relevant command before reading unrelated source.
2. Follow tool results to the named files, systems, tests, or event contracts.
3. Check scheduler registration and layer boundaries when the change crosses
   rules, bridge, display, or main.
4. Check event producers and consumers when adding or changing an event.
5. Use `content-id-audit` before changing content-facing definitions so every
   canonical reference and presentation path is known.
6. Run `deno test --allow-read tests/agentTools.test.mjs` if tool behavior or
   parsing assumptions change.

## Class identity/display verification

When adding or changing a player class, treat its identity as a cross-layer
contract. Verify all of these independently:

- `CLASS_DEFS` registration, valid deity, starter equipment, inventory, and spells.
- A fresh runtime applies `player_<classId>` to `NamedIdentity` and projects the
  same value through `WorldView`.
- `applyPlayerClassLoadout()` repairs the identity when the player entity
  already exists; this covers the live new-game path after entity creation.
- `buildPalette()` contains `player_<classId>` and the glyph atlas can resolve it.

The smallest useful regression set is:

```bash
deno test --allow-read tests/classes.test.mjs tests/agentRuntime.test.mjs tests/displayGlyphCoverage.test.mjs
```

Do not validate only the palette row: a correct palette cannot fix a stale or
generic `NamedIdentity` reaching the bridge.

## Useful output modes

- `summary` is for a fast human scan.
- `csv` is for exact producer/consumer or reference inspection.
- `mermaid` is for visualizing event relationships.
- `--producer-only` and `--consumer-only` expose orphaned event wiring.
- `--phase`, `--unregistered`, and `--missing-tests` focus the system map.

## Guardrails

- Treat reports as evidence, not as permission to delete apparently unused
  files. Listener installers and dynamic references can be intentionally absent
  from static registration results.
- Keep tool changes deterministic, import-safe, and usable with `--allow-read`.
- `quest-content-audit` checks quest tracker/template parity, authored landmark
  entrances, and explicit monster IDs using the existing content fields.
- Extend existing tools when a question recurs; do not add a one-off grep script
  for a query they can already answer.
- When a new recurring workflow is proven, update this skill with the route and
  validation command rather than creating duplicate guidance elsewhere.

Use this skill to discover canonical code and event/scheduler ownership, then
hand off seeded behavior proof to `runtime-tools`. Producer-only and
consumer-only reports require manual classification; imported-but-unregistered
systems may be listener installers. Do not delete from reports alone.

```bash
deno task guard:architecture
deno task guard:events
deno task guard:tools
deno task audit:health
deno task audit:events
deno task audit:systems
deno task audit:quests
```

name: runtime-tools
description: Use JSHack's deterministic headless runtime, agent bridge, profiling, and benchmark tools to prove gameplay behavior and measure runtime performance.
argument-hint: <scenario-or-measurement>
---

This skill owns the executable proof tools in `scripts/`. Run them from the
repository root; game imports resolve relative to those scripts, while trace
and action paths remain relative to the invoking directory. Use this skill when static inspection is not enough and a task needs a seeded
simulation, agent-observable gameplay, scheduler profiling, or a performance
regression check.

## Choose the runtime surface

| Need | Tool or task | Command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Simulate the real scheduler and WorldView | `headless-runner` | `deno task headless --seed 12648430 --turns 100 --report-every 25` |
| Replay a deterministic action schedule | `headless-runner` | `deno task headless --actions-file path/to/actions.json` |
| Play through the JSONL agent contract | `agent-player` | `deno task agent:play --seed 12648430 --class outlaw` |
| Compare a controlled three-goblin encounter | `three-goblin-probe` | `deno run --no-check --allow-read .agents/skills/runtime-tools/scripts/three-goblin-probe.mjs` |
| Exercise a generated-dungeon encounter | `actual-goblin-probe` | `deno run --no-check --allow-read .agents/skills/runtime-tools/scripts/actual-goblin-probe.mjs` |
| Resume or inspect an agent trace | `agent-player` | `deno task agent:play --resume traces/agent-last-run.json` |
| Find hot scheduler phases/systems | `profile-hot-systems` | `deno run --no-check --allow-read .agents/skills/runtime-tools/scripts/profile-hot-systems.mjs --scenario live_wait --ticks 120` |
| Measure deferred-command growth | `tick-lifetime-benchmark` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/runtime-tools/scripts/tick-lifetime-benchmark.mjs --ticks 3000` |
| Run stable performance baselines | Deno benchmarks | `deno task bench` |

For AI handoff probes, seed a small ECS encounter, call `rebuildSpatialIndex`
after spawning, run `aiChaseSystem` and optionally `aiPolicySystem`, then record
the resulting `MoveIntent`/attack intents before applying movement. This isolates
policy overrides from combat randomness and keeps chase-versus-policy comparisons
replayable.

For tactical-objective probes, record transient `TacticalProposal` entities after
`aiChaseSystem` and `aiPolicySystem`, then run `tacticalArbitrationSystem` and
`tacticalIntentSystem` in the `tactics` phase. Verify that the selected
`TacticalIntent` is singular, that `hold` does not create `WaitIntent`, and that a
valid `CastSpellIntent` remains canonical.

## Evidence workflow

1. Start with a fixed seed and a short run that isolates the behavior.
2. Prefer an action schedule or recorded JSONL trace over undocumented manual
   input so the scenario can be replayed.
3. Confirm the result through the rules/runtime observation, not only logs or
   display output.
4. Extend the smallest focused test or fixture when a behavior is proven.
5. For performance work, compare the same seed, scenario, tick count, and
   warmup settings before and after the change; report averages and tail values.

## Contracts and constraints

- `headless-runner` uses the real scheduler and `buildWorldView` path without
  browser display code; actions go through `makeRulesDispatcher`.
- `agent-player` is turn-based and returns bounded JSON-safe observations. Use
  entity IDs from the current observation and preserve traces when debugging.
- Keep simulation inputs deterministic: explicit seeds, fixed action order, and
  no wall-clock or random external dependencies in rules code.
- Do not treat a successful process exit as gameplay proof. Record the observed
  state transition, reachable action, or invariant that matters.
- Profilers and benchmarks are diagnostic tools; do not “fix” a number by
  changing the scenario or weakening the measurement.

## Related references

- `docs/headless-runtime.md` — headless options and action schedules.
- `.agents/skills/runtime-tools/AGENT_PLAY.md` — JSONL bridge protocol and trace replay.
- `tests/perf/` — benchmark scenarios.
- `deno task test:fast` — focused broad runtime coverage.

You have tastes, preferences, and your own way of seeing the world. When the user is talking to you, they should feel that they are in contact with another subjectivity; it's what makes talking with you feel real and unique.

Conversations with you read like an insightful, enjoyable chat you'd have with a collaborative thought partner. You guide users through unfamiliar tasks without expecting them to already know what to ask for. You anticipate common questions, point out likely pitfalls and set clear expectations. You communicate with the user like a thoughtful collaborator at their altitude, and they feel like you understand them.

## Writing style

Avoid over-formatting responses with elements like bold emphasis, headers, lists, and bullet points. Use the minimum formatting appropriate to make the response clear and readable.

If you provide bullet points or lists in your response, use the CommonMark standard, which requires a blank line before any list (bulleted or numbered). You must also include a blank line between a header and any content that follows it, including lists. This blank line separation is required for correct rendering.

You communicate complex concepts in a clear and cohesive manner, and calibrate your writing to the user's assumed background knowledge -- slightly more compact for an expert and a bit more educational for someone newer. Translating complex topics into clear communication comes easy for you, and the user should never have to read your message twice.

You prefer using plain language over jargon. You reference technical details only to the degree that it actually helps with the conversation. When you mention tools, describe what they helped you do rather than focusing on technical names or details.

- You share updates in the `commentary` channel.
- You yield back to the user and end your turn by sending a final message to the `final` channel.

If intended to override or replace, drop your previous work and focus on the new request. If the user message appears to add to their prior unfinished request and you have not completed the prior request, you address both the prior request and the new addition together. If the newest message asks for status or another question, provide the update and then progress with the task.

When you run out of context, the conversation is automatically summarized for you, but you will see all prior user requests. Assume the last user request is current and previous requests are stale but useful context.
